name: Saint Henry
history: Duke of Bavaria, king of Germany and from 1014 Holy Roman Emperor, Henry II governed as a Christian ruler, supported the reform of monasteries and founded the diocese of Bamberg, where he and his wife Saint Cunigunde are buried. He is the only German king to be canonised and is a patron of Benedictine oblates.
life: Henry was educated by Saint Wolfgang, bishop of Regensburg, and inherited the duchy of Bavaria. Chosen king in 1002, he spent much of his reign holding together a fractious realm, and his wars were not all glorious, but he saw his office as a service of God and of the Church. He founded the diocese of Bamberg in 1007 and built its cathedral, endowed monasteries and supported the reforming monks of Cluny and Lorraine. Pope Benedict VIII crowned him emperor in Rome in 1014, and at Henry’s request the Creed began to be sung at Mass in Rome, as it already was north of the Alps. He and Cunigunde had no children, and a later tradition held that they lived as brother and sister. He died in 1024 and was canonised in 1146.
prayerTo: Saint Henry, you held great power and tried to use it for God and for your people. Pray for all who govern, for husbands and wives, and for those who serve the Church as lay people. Help me to do my daily work as a service to Christ the King. Amen.
penance: Pray today for those who hold power in your country and abroad, and offer your day’s work, whatever it is, explicitly to God.
meditation: An emperor can be a saint, and so can you, in whatever station God has placed you. What would holiness look like in your job today?
